textbookText: A. Tick the correct alternative. 1. Why are viruses considered obligate parasites? a. They required a living host to multiply b. They can survive independently outside a host c. They possess their own enzyme system d. They are capable of photosynthesis 2. What is the significance of the term ‘bacteriophage’? a. It refers to a bacterium that infects higher plant cells. b. It denotes a bacterium that infects an animal cell. c. It represents a virus that infects a bacterium. d. It describes an organelle of a bacterium. 3. Which statement is not true for viruses? a. Viruses are made of proteins and nucleic acid. b. Viruses can multiply only in living cells. c. Viruses can grow in dilute sugary syrups in warm weather. d. Viruses cannot use oxygen. 4. Which components are typically found in viruses? a. DNA and protein b. Proteins, RNA and DNA c. RNA and DNA d. Proteins and RNA or DNA 5. What is the primary component of the capsid structure found in viruses? a. protein b. proteins and carbohydrates c. proteins and DNA d. proteins and RNA B. Answer the following questions: 1. Define virus and Explain why they are considered neither prokaryotes nor eukaryotes. 2. What is capsid? 3. Discuss the characteristics of viruses that place them midway between living and nonliving things. 4. How do viruses differ from bacteria in terms of their cell structure, reproduction, and nuclear substance? 5. Describe the economic importance of the virus. 6. Explain the structure of the virus with an appropriate diagram. 7. How do viruses use lysozyme to interact with host cells, and what is its role in the infection process?

Project Work: Prepare a report on any one viral disease (like, HIV/AIDs, Influence, COVID -19 etc.) by including symptoms, transmission, preventive methods and societal, economic and healthcare impact. Present your finding in class.
